title: A container with a size of its own can cut off what does not fit
goal: A screen cuts off anything hanging over its edge. A card, a button or any other container given a size does not: a long title runs straight out the side of the card and is still there in the export. The same switch a screen already has belongs on any container that has been given a size.
notes: Most of this exists. GroupContent already stores clipsContents on EVERY group; only Layer.clipsToFrame (Layer.swift:769) narrows it to group?.isFrame == true, and Document.swift:251 plus ComponentPieceEditing.swift:173 gate hit testing on the same property. The renderer path is DocumentRenderer.swift:489, `layer.clipsToFrame ? layer.localBounds : layer.renderBounds`. The switch itself is in FrameInspector.swift; putting it on a sized group means the Layout section carries it, not the Frame section. Comes from queue/audits/2026-09-04-starter-sizing.json: 'A text field with a long placeholder wraps and gets taller instead of truncating with an ellipsis, because a text layer has nothing that clips it.' Truncating words with an ellipsis is a separate, later question: this task is only about the box cutting off what leaves it. Also the honest partner to the pending task a-container-can-be-told-the-smallest-and-largest, whose acceptance says a stack pinned at its largest size must not overflow quietly.
acceptance: A group that has been given a width or a height offers the same Clip contents switch a screen offers, in the same words and the same place in the panel
With it on, anything past the edge is not drawn, not clicked and not exported, and rounded corners cut with the corner rather than the square box
It is off by default for a group, so nothing in an existing picture changes until somebody turns it on, and a group that closes around its contents is not offered it at all
A copy takes the setting from its original, the same way it takes the rest of the arrangement

Ships behind next-auto-layout. To see it: open Photonz Next, drop the starter card, give it a height of 120, watch the text run past the bottom, then turn Clip contents on and watch it stop at the edge
Tests in PhotonzCore cover drawing, hit testing and export with clipping on and off, written before any app code
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The switch must NOT be offered on a group that closes around its contents: there is nothing hanging out of it, and a control that changes nothing is worse than no control. Offered only where the box is a size somebody gave it: a width, a height, or a largest size (a max caps the box in GroupFlow.size via layout.held, so contents overflow there too). (2) Off by default is not free: GroupContent.clipsContents is stored on EVERY group and defaults to true, so reusing it as-is would silently start clipping every sized group in every saved document. The setting becomes optional (nil = nobody has said), read as 'a screen clips, a group does not'. (3) Cut from the mock/notes: no new visual affordance, no per-axis clipping, no ellipsis. Same checkbox, same two words, in the Layout section right under Width and Height, where the number that caused the overflow was just typed. (4) Real cost to name: a plain group that clips stops being a pass-through in the renderer, so a child set to multiply inside it blends against the group instead of the canvas. That is the same trade a screen already makes, and it only happens once somebody turns the switch on. (5) A copy is shown the setting, never asked it, like every other thing on its arrangement.

Built. Model: GroupContent's clipsContents becomes an optional setting (nil = nobody has said), read as 'a screen cuts off, a group does not', so every saved document opens drawing exactly what it drew. GroupLayout.hasSizeOfItsOwn (a width, a height or a ceiling) and Layer.hasBoxOfItsOwn decide who is offered it; Layer.clipsToFrame became Layer.clipsToBounds and now covers both kinds. Renderer: a plain group that clips stops being a pass-through (DocumentRenderer.swift compositeLayers) so there is a buffer to cut at, and the buffer IS the box. Hit testing already went through clipsToFrame in Document.hitTestPath and ComponentPieceEditing, plus a new arm in Layer.contains for a group (which is still not a surface: its empty room takes no click). RenderDiff repaints a clipping container when its box moves. PhotonzDocument.setFrameClips became setClipsContents. App: a checkbox in the Layout section under Width and Height (ArrangementInspector.clipRow), and a clause in a copy's sentence, since a copy is shown this and never asked it. 13 core tests + 3 render tests, written first.

Found and fixed a real bug underneath. On the live canvas the card came out cut at roughly half size while the offscreen render was right: Layer.magnified scales frames and styles but was leaving group.layout alone, so a group that arranges itself measured its own box in document points while its children were measured in output pixels. Fixed in DocumentMagnification.swift (GroupLayout.magnified, GroupPadding.magnified) with a test. This was latent before today: a laid-out group's corner radius and border have been drawing at the wrong box on a zoomed canvas since layouts landed.

Adversarial review of the built thing, on the real app (Scripts/playtest/clip-contents-walk.json, Screen Recording granted so the shots are real captures). What works: the switch appears exactly where the number that caused the overflow was typed, the cut is clean, the click through the cut-away words picks nothing, and unticking brings everything back untouched. What I could not fix here: a cut-away child still looks like any other row in the Layers list with nothing saying it is off screen - filed as a-container-says-when-it-is-hiding-something-you, which covers screens too since they have always had the same gap.
